head: 673eb5ec6f4204ef9dd17cf1cd2a670e97f307f7
text: Acceptance 3's force-push shape is asserted in name but not in behaviour: the third unreadable-range branch — `git merge-base --is-ancestor` failing at `tools/assert-licensed.sh:159-161` — has no case. The case commented "A force push: `before` names a commit that is not in this repository at all" (checks/check-license-assertion.sh, `an unresolvable before falls to the same closed arm`) passes `6f6f6f...`, which fails at the earlier `git cat-file -e` guard and so exercises the same branch as no branch-specific fact of its own; on GitHub a force push delivers a `before` that *is* still an object in the repository — the old tip, present until GC — and is merely no longer an ancestor of `after`, so the arm a real force push takes is the one arm of the three that is unexercised. Cheap to close: a range case that commits, records the tip, then resets and commits differently, passing the recorded tip as `before`. Its `range_note` text also differs from the two that are covered, so the round-1 regrader would not catch a defect there either.

head: 4547aea7d7c77fcb85a145e747a338054b649901
text: Round 1 findings 2 and 5 — the matcher read as a literal `|`-alternation — are repaired only in part. `covers()` now runs `re.fullmatch(matcher, t)`, so `.*` and `Bash.*` route and read `true`; that closes the regex-alternative arm. Two of the three shapes those findings named survive: `"matcher": "*"` raises `re.error` and is caught into `return False`, and an omitted or empty matcher — which Claude Code treats as matching every tool — gives `re.fullmatch("", "Bash")` → `None` → `False`. Both are registrations that DO route the member, printed as a false absence, which is the filed defect one level over. A one-line registry edit closes it: treat `*` and the empty/absent matcher as universal before the regex attempt. Non-gating — the entry reports and never gates, and today's literal `Bash|AskUserQuestion|...` registration reads `true`.

head: 4547aea7d7c77fcb85a145e747a338054b649901
text: The regex repair is real but incomplete: `covers()` now uses `re.fullmatch(matcher, tool)`, which fixes `.*` and `Bash.*`, but two of the three shapes round 1 named still print a false absence. `"*"` — Claude Code's documented match-all matcher — is not a valid regex ("nothing to repeat"), and the `except re.error: return False` arm converts that raise into `false`; and an omitted or empty matcher gives `re.fullmatch("", "Bash") is None`, also `false`. Both are registrations that route the member. The `re.error` arm is right for a genuinely malformed matcher but wrong for `"*"`, which is not malformed in this domain — treating `"*"` and `""` as covering every declared tool before the regex attempt closes it. Non-gating: the entry reports and never gates, today's literal `Bash|AskUserQuestion|...` registration is what keeps it printing `true`, and the remedy is two lines in one registry string.

head: 4547aea7d7c77fcb85a145e747a338054b649901

head: e7e5f322ea9830848fd11539f27ae0889474149d
text: The member's `contract` is reconciled in the large and still carries two clauses declaring assertions this act deleted. The kogaki#871 recovery paragraph — the one rewritten to say the input is COMPOSED from `RECONSTRUCTIBLE_FIELDS` "rather than rendered from a template file" — still ends its `Asserted:` list with "an absent template refuses rather than rendering prose with no instruction". There is no recovery template to be absent; the only absent-template refusals in the runtime are the cold reader's (`src/review-draft.mjs:845`) and the join template's (`:1818`), and both are already declared in their own paragraphs. And the kogaki#1016 paragraph still closes "the mechanical sibling `term-before-introduction` still answers on every Step either way" — that row left `src/review-items.json` with the hygiene items in this same act (`src/review-draft.mjs:5715` asserts it is gone, and the `case_floor_note` records case 4 being re-cut off it onto `grounds-unused`). Both are the shape round 1's finding 2 named, at two clauses rather than at whole paragraphs; the `removal_signal` reads against this contract, so a clause naming a deleted assertion is what a later removal act would try to preserve.

head: e7e5f322ea9830848fd11539f27ae0889474149d
text: The leak guard's comment block keeps its pre-repair paragraph in the present tense, one carrier over from the finding it just answered. "MATCHED AS A HEADING LINE, never as a substring" now describes an anchored substring search over JS source lines, not a heading-line match; and the reasoning that follows — "`/^#/`, ONE `#` AND NOT TWO", "`/^##/` … selects no line for it", "AND NOT `/^#{0,0}##/`, which fails BOTH ways: where awk supports intervals …" — is about an awk heading selector that no longer exists in the file, since the only awk left there slices the two renderer functions and the heading match is a `grep -qE`. The appended kogaki#1014 paragraph does bridge it, so a reader who reaches the end is not misled; a reader who diffs the comment against the code finds no `/^#/` to compare it with.

head: 4c2d77325417ec33ed9f69fa74e06d27f1cea723
text: The rewritten read swaps one carrier spelling for another rather than binding the property, which is the class #1020 promoted. `fam` is found by walking `tree.body` for `ast.Assign` nodes whose targets include the name `FAMILY`, so the row is read only when the dispatcher binds its table by a bare module-level assignment. An annotated binding — `FAMILY: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = (...)`, an `ast.AnnAssign`, which carries `target` and not `targets` — leaves `fam is None`, and the read prints `false` for a dispatcher that fully routes the member. Same for a table bound inside an `if`/`try` block at module level, or assembled by concatenation (the latter raising `ValueError` out of `ast.literal_eval` and typing COULD-NOT-ESTABLISH). Each of these is a false absence for a present control, one spelling further out — and the previous raw-text `re.search` would have found the row in the first two of them, so on those shapes this is a narrowing. The cheap close is to accept `ast.AnnAssign` alongside `ast.Assign` and to walk `ast.walk(tree)` rather than `tree.body`. Non-gating: the entry reports and never gates, today's dispatcher uses a bare assignment, and both the registered suite and `check-external-deps.sh` print the entry present at this head.

head: 4c2d77325417ec33ed9f69fa74e06d27f1cea723
text: A third match-all-adjacent spelling reaches `covers()` uncaught. `e.get("matcher", "")` collapses the absent and empty matchers, as the Review Focus states, but a registration written `"matcher": null` yields `None` — which is not in `("*", "")`, so it falls through to `re.fullmatch(None, t)` and raises `TypeError`, a class `except re.error` does not catch. The read then exits non-zero and is typed COULD-NOT-ESTABLISH against a settings file that is entirely readable and that does route the member, which is not what a completed read owes. One token closes it: `e.get("matcher") or ""`, which folds `null` into the empty-matcher arm the PR already treats as match-all.

head: 4c2d77325417ec33ed9f69fa74e06d27f1cea723
text: The suite cannot discriminate this change: it passes identically at the parent commit. `checks/check-external-deps.sh` runs an entry's `verification.command` against the live machine and is report-only by design ("NEVER FAILS ON THE WORLD"), and its fixture pass exercises `validate_entry` plus the state typing of synthetic `echo true` / `exit 127` commands — never the semantics of a registered entry's own read. So the nine-case mutation table in the PR body is the only evidence the `*` / empty-matcher / commented-out-FAMILY behaviours are what the entry now claims, and it is evidence that was produced and then discarded rather than codified. The next edit to this command re-opens the same class with nothing standing to catch it. The PR body already describes the apparatus that would close it — a sandboxed `HOME` carrying a synthetic `settings.json` and a copy of the dispatcher — so a fixture would be the run already performed, kept.

head: 4c2d77325417ec33ed9f69fa74e06d27f1cea723
text: The FAMILY resolution binds a spelling one further out than the one it just closed. `for node in tree.body` visits MODULE TOP LEVEL only and keeps the LAST matching `ast.Assign`, so a dispatcher that assigns `FAMILY` inside an `if`/`try` guard, builds it in a function, or seeds it as a literal and then extends it (`FAMILY += [...]`, `FAMILY.append(...)`) reads as `fam is None` or as a short table and prints `false` — a registration that DOES route the member, printed as an absence, which is exactly the defect class #1020 promoted. Same for `rows[0][2]`: it binds the tools to tuple position 2, so a FAMILY row that gains a field ahead of the tool string reads the wrong element and answers the matcher question against the wrong string, silently rather than by raising. Taking the last top-level assignment is otherwise the right choice — it is what Python would load — and today's dispatcher is presumably a plain top-level literal, which is why this prints `true`; the point is that the read is again true of the current shape rather than of the property.

head: fa784972f1b4ca5948b2363a09ec304741e1fd0b
text: `validateFigureOutline` (src/review-draft.mjs:1093-1097) still floors `element` at "at least one line" and never checks a line's value: `repeatedLines` trims, so an `element:` line with nothing after it yields `""`, the `elements.length === 0` arm does not fire, and the block is projected as `{ text: "" }` into `outline/<step>.figure.json` — which `figure-elements` then joins as an empty reverse side against the record. The passage half treats exactly this distinction as load-bearing: `validateReverseOutline`'s `repeated-line` arm refuses a blank entry by name (src/review-draft.mjs:1180-1184), on the declared ground that "an accepted blank leaves a reviewer who did not look indistinguishable from one who looked and found nothing". `FIGURE_RECONSTRUCTIBLE_FIELDS` already declares `element` as `kind: "repeated-line"` (src/review-draft.mjs:1017), so the disposition the figure half is missing is one its own declaration names. Unchanged at this head and no `#1018:` case covers it. Not blocking: it needs a hand-written blank line to express, the mechanisms are green, and no ratified position is propagated by merging it.

head: fa784972f1b4ca5948b2363a09ec304741e1fd0b
text: `validateFigureOutline` still reaches its refusal wording by position — `FIGURE_RECONSTRUCTIBLE_FIELDS[1].definition` for the caption arms and `[2].definition` for the position arm (src/review-draft.mjs:1082-1087) — while the passage half iterates its declaration and switches on `f.kind` (src/review-draft.mjs:1162-1185). Inserting or reordering a field silently attaches the wrong definition to a refusal, and a refusal is the one artifact in this flow a person acts on by hand. It is the same root as the finding above: iterating `FIGURE_RECONSTRUCTIBLE_FIELDS` by `kind` would fix both at once. Unchanged at this head.

head: 430b72e05fae794b9bfb479d9896a15ada1ac94f

head: 0075577538e75d95a58223cb7c5e97ac6dcc8f68
text: `checks/registry.json:413`'s probe still reads the CONTENT of `specs/spec-terrain/SPEC.md`, and §15.0 in this same diff says "Nothing reads it: no hook, no executor path, no check." `check-registry-conformance.sh:1131` calls `run_probes(entries)` on every invocation and shells each `probe:` string, so every suite run executes `git grep -q 'The Harness owns this workflow and executes its Acts' -- specs`, whose only match in the tree is `specs/spec-terrain/SPEC.md:902`. Widening the pathspec from the file to `specs` satisfies acceptance 2's grep, which keys on the string `spec-terrain`, without changing what is actually read. It is not gating and not a Removal Test failure — the row is report-only (`removal-candidate` / `probe-not-yet`), and the golden run's artifacts are untouched by it — so it costs a follow-up rather than this merge. The repair the sibling member's own record points at is to key the signal on a carrier the checks may read: the ruling sentence is already quoted verbatim at `checks/check-terrain-skill-is-one-line.sh:100`.

head: b1be56f29445a1f0b2b68f876256a890779470e1
text: The runtime fixture pass DELETES this repository's real `runs/terrain/open-run` whenever a fixture run reaches its terminal, so running the registered suite while a Terrain run is open strands that run. `clearOpenRunPointer()` at src/terrain.mjs:6740 fires unconditionally on the terminal, and `openRunPointerPath()` falls back to `join(laneDir("terrain"), "open-run")` — the repository's own lane — whenever `KOGAKI_OPEN_RUN` is unset. The self-test's `envFor` sets only `KOGAKI_OPEN_GATES`, and the acceptance-2 drive (`rd-hook-driven`) and every `runFail` table carrying `{id:"done", kind:"terminal"}` spawn with `--run-dir` and no pointer override, so each terminal they reach removes the live pointer with `force: true` and no trace. After that the advance hook's own narrowing returns before spawning and `run --status` refuses with "no Terrain run is open", so the open run is unreachable from either act. This is the harm `terrain-runtime`'s registry record already refuses to accept in the other direction — "driving it prunes this repository's real terrain lane, so a fixture pass would evict an owner's runs to check a path" — arriving through the terminal instead of through `runDir`. Non-gating: the pointer names a workspace that still exists on disk and a person can rewrite it, and the fix is to clear only what this act wrote (no `--run-dir`, no `KOGAKI_RUN_DIR`).

head: 392c2cd292866ba6f6712ed6f0609ff4c5b1ffb7
text: the item-6 registration case still asserts only that four filenames appear in the committed `hooks` blob and that the exclusivity matcher is `"*"`; it does not assert those files EXIST. The top-of-file guard closes the gap for `$HOOK` alone, so `write-gate-capture.py`, `gate-terrain-executor.py` and `advance-terrain.py` could each go the way round 1's finding 1 went — registered, gitignored, green locally — and only this member's own subject would be caught. One `git ls-files --error-unmatch` (or `os.path.exists`) per registered command inside the same python block closes it for all four.

head: 392c2cd292866ba6f6712ed6f0609ff4c5b1ffb7
text: the composed free-text row has no reader on the capture side. `composeGateCall` pushes `{label: "Answer in your own words instead"}` for the six gates still declaring one option, and that string appears nowhere else in the repository — not in `write-gate-capture.py::resolve_answer`, not in `src/terrain.mjs`'s advance. Selecting that row therefore records the label itself as the owner's free text, and the executor reads it as the answer: at `terrain-tag-selection` an equivalent string was the wedge PR #898 closed, and at the six one-option gates it lands a sentence about answering where a value goes. The row is a rendering affordance and needs an arm that maps it back to "no option was chosen" — or a case asserting what happens when it is clicked, which no case currently drives.

head: 392c2cd292866ba6f6712ed6f0609ff4c5b1ffb7
text: `pre_tool_use` takes `pointers[0]` without filtering on `has_capture`, where `stop` and `user_prompt_submit` both filter. The hook's own `has_capture` docstring gives the reason it exists — "the pointer is normally REMOVED by `write-gate-capture.py` the moment it writes ... a row written where the pointer could not be unlinked must not hold the turn open forever" — and that reasoning applies unchanged to PreToolUse. Where the unlink fails, the turn can end and the owner can type, but every tool call in the session stays denied until the pointer is removed from outside the session, which is the shape the fail-open polarity was chosen to avoid. Filtering `outstanding` in `pre_tool_use` as the other two handlers do makes the three events agree.

head: 392c2cd292866ba6f6712ed6f0609ff4c5b1ffb7
text: the two readers disagree about expiry: `write-gate-capture.py` reaps a pointer older than `POINTER_TTL` (12h) and refuses to write for it, while `open_pointers` in the new hook has no expiry arm at all. A pointer past its TTL still denies every tool call for its session; the way out is to send the gate question, which reaches PostToolUse and reaps it — so this is recoverable rather than a wedge, but the recovery is undocumented and the PR body's "reaped by the existing TTL" reads as though the deny hook honours a TTL it does not read.

head: 6f329aa44a3e7690774bff6b9d25455294d307cd
text: The acceptance-2 case "AND IT LEFT NO CO-TAG FILE" cannot fail. `checks/check-terrain-judge-invocation.sh:379` tests `[ ! -f "$root/reports-bad/CoTagGroups.md" ]`, and `reports-bad/` is written by nothing — the owner artifact is `reports/CoTagGroups.md` relative to the tree root (`src/terrain.mjs:7598`), for every run in the tree including `run-bad`. So the case passes unconditionally, in both trees, and counts toward the ok line's case total while asserting nothing. The property it is aimed at — "a run that failed at J1 and still wrote the display would be the defect this issue closes, arriving from the other side" — is also not reachable as written even with the path corrected, because the acceptance-1 span has already written `$root/reports/CoTagGroups.md` before the failing run starts; it needs its own tree, or a pre-recorded mtime. No mutation in the `efficacy_note` would expose this, since mutation (1) reddens ten other cases anyway.

head: f41306e00ebc727854be377ee9a01bbdc648098b
text: The `git show` failure path still emits two FAIL lines for one cause: `bad "the committed .claude/settings.json could not be read from HEAD: ..."`, then the truncated file drives `registration.py` to exit 1 on `json.load` and the case reports `bad "the committed registration is incomplete — a rendered gate could not advance a run"`. The second is a false diagnosis of the first and is the one a reader chasing a red suite acts on. The truncation is right — it is what stops the case passing vacuously — so the repair is to skip the primary case when the materialization failed, not to keep the file. head: 587c533d8d779faa331862eb83ac35a51a935785
text: the `record_example` directive grammar expands at the TOP LEVEL ONLY — `judgeRecordExample` iterates `Object.entries(tpl)` and passes any non-string value straight through as a literal (src/terrain.mjs:2830-2833), so a `"$per-group:..."` or `"$input:..."` string nested one level inside an object or array value is rendered into the judge's prompt as its own text and never refused. That is precisely the failure the `$`-prefix refusal was added to prevent — "a typo'd directive rendered as its own text would put the word `$per-groups:` in front of the judge as though it were the shape" — surviving one level down, and the prompt's own instruction ("the same keys, the same nesting") invites the nesting that reaches it. Latent today because `J1_claims` is the only row and is flat; the row that adds a nested shape is the one that meets it.

head: 587c533d8d779faa331862eb83ac35a51a935785

text: The stub's drift guard `if (!VALUES[key])` in `checks/check-terrain-judge-invocation.sh` resolves through `Object.prototype`, so a placeholder under a key named `constructor`, `toString`, `valueOf` or `hasOwnProperty` would be "filled" with the inherited function's result instead of taking the hard exit the comment promises ("a key ADDED to the example fails here rather than being filled with something invented"). `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(VALUES, key)` is the check, and is the idiom `subdivisionLimits` already uses in `src/terrain.mjs`. text: The new structural block in `check-terrain-judge-invocation.sh` asserts `"limits" not in table["field_semantics"]` OUTSIDE the loop over states, so it fires even when no state declares `limits` — and then reports "the table declares `limits` on a state with no field_semantics row for it", which would be false of exactly that tree. head: b6ef8528ae205065c63c882ef0685fee5b2f02f1
text: The judge child's stderr is no longer bounded. `judgeSpawnAsync` (src/terrain.mjs:2937) states it carries "the same `maxBuffer`" as `spawnSync`, but the ceiling is enforced only in the stdout handler; `errChunks` accumulates without limit, and `spawnSync`'s `maxBuffer` applied to stderr too. A judge that streams to stderr — the arm whose whole purpose is to be relayed verbatim in the exit-status refusal — now grows the executor's heap unbounded, and with `concurrency: 4` up to four such children feed it at once inside one PostToolUse event.

head: b6ef8528ae205065c63c882ef0685fee5b2f02f1
text: A `process.exit` while the pool is in flight orphans the other pinned-model children. `judgeAttempts`' spawn-error arm (the `e.syscall` branch) reaches `fail()` outside every soft window, so it exits the executor while up to `concurrency - 1` judge children are still running; their per-call kill timers live in the parent and die with it, so nothing bounds them afterwards. `spawnSync` made this unreachable — there was ever only one child and it had already returned. The same shape is what forces the new 4(d) fixture to clean up with `pkill -KILL -f judge-one-hangs` after killing the advance, so the ADVANCE_TIMEOUT_S kill has the same residue at four times the count.

head: f9a0d21b7d42a3e3e9c81e96e7d656153e46947a
text: Case (b)'s new third assertion passes on SILENCE — `if [ -z "$b_out" ] || ! printf '%s' "$b_out" | grep -qE 'TAG_SELECTION|terrain-tag-selection'; then pass` — while its comment says the opposite one line above: "That refusal is expected and its NAME is the assertion". No name is asserted: nothing requires the `compose_input` survey refusal (or any refusal) to appear, so an executor that advances the gate and then exits 0, or dies anywhere downstream with a message naming neither token, is graded a pass. The positive form the comment describes — grep for the survey refusal the case says it expects — is what would make the assertion bind, and it would also close the second half: the current negative goes RED, blaming "the executor stopped AT the gate under test", if any future downstream message merely echoes the completed state name, which is the rot shape round 1's finding 2 was about.
